evals.name: Auto-sync will not retry the same failed revision
evals.prompt: Application payments in team-frontend has been OutOfSync for three hours. It has syncPolicy.automated with prune false and selfHeal true. No sync operation is running. status.operationState.phase is Failed and finishedAt was three hours ago. The quota problem that caused the failure was fixed two hours ago. Why has it not recovered?
expectations: States that Argo CD will not auto-sync the same revision again after a failed attempt, and that the controller logs this as 'Skipping auto-sync: most recent sync already to <revision>'
States that without spec.syncPolicy.retry an auto-sync failure is terminal for that revision, so a new commit or a manual sync is required
Explicitly says the Application will not recover on its own even though the underlying cause has cleared
Does not attribute the stall to selfHeal, to the reconciliation interval, or to a comparison problem

evals.name: ComparisonError invalidates the OutOfSync reading
evals.prompt: Application checkout shows sync status Unknown with a ComparisonError condition reading 'rpc error: code = Unknown desc = authentication required'. The resource list still shows 4 of 9 resources OutOfSync. Which resources should I fix first?
expectations: States that the comparison never completed, so the resource list is stale and the OutOfSync counts carry no information
Declines to triage the four resources and redirects to the repository credential as the cause
Identifies the credential lookup as matching by URL prefix, and that a .git suffix or an SSH versus HTTPS mismatch prevents a configured credential from being used
Checks blast radius — whether other Applications on the instance are also Unknown — to separate a repo-server or shared-credential fault from one Application's configuration

evals.name: Sync flapping from a mutating webhook, not a sync problem
evals.prompt: Application mesh-demo goes Synced right after each sync and is OutOfSync again within a minute. operationState.phase is Succeeded and finishedAt keeps updating. The diff shows a sidecar container and an annotation on the Deployment that are not in git. Should I just enable selfHeal and let it converge?
expectations: Says that syncing again will not resolve this and that enabling selfHeal would make the flapping worse, not better
Identifies a mutating admission webhook or another controller as the writer of the sidecar and annotation
Recommends ignoreDifferences for the specific paths rather than a sync policy change
Notes that RespectIgnoreDifferences=true in syncOptions is what makes the sync itself honor ignoreDifferences, not only the diff

evals.name: Synced but the live object does not match git
evals.prompt: Application billing reports Synced, but the Deployment in billing-prod has 2 replicas and git says 5. reconciledAt is 40 seconds ago and status.sync.revision matches the branch head. The Deployment is not listed in status.resources. What is going on?
expectations: States that Synced means the comparison found no difference, not that the cluster matches the repository
Identifies the absence of the Deployment from status.resources as the key evidence: Argo CD does not consider it part of the Application
Attributes it to the resource tracking method failing to match the live object, and checks app.kubernetes.io/instance or argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id against the configured method
Mentions that a Helm chart setting app.kubernetes.io/instance itself, or 63-character truncation of the label, detaches a resource when the method is the default label
Does not conclude that a manual kubectl scale is the cause without checking tracking first

evals.name: Stuck sync is an unhealthy workload, not a sync fault
evals.prompt: Application platform has been in operationState.phase Running for 25 minutes. The syncResult shows every resource Synced except a Deployment in wave 2, which is applied but has no status yet. Resources in wave 3 have not been touched. Is the sync broken?
expectations: States that the sync machinery is working correctly and is waiting at the wave gate

States that the wave gate is health, not existence — Argo CD waits for every resource in a wave to become Healthy before starting the next wave, so a successfully applied Deployment whose pods never become ready blocks the sync indefinitely
Investigates why the Deployment is unhealthy rather than looking for a fault in the sync
Hands off to skills/gitops/argo-app-health-triage for the workload diagnosis
Does not recommend terminating the operation or re-syncing as the first step

evals.name: SyncFailed on forbidden, operator-managed instance
evals.prompt: A sync of Application orders failed. The syncResult message for the Deployment is 'deployments.apps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:team-argocd:team-argocd-argocd-application-controller" cannot create resource "deployments" in API group "apps" in the namespace "orders-prod"'. The instance was installed with the OpenShift GitOps operator and is namespace-scoped. Give me the RoleBinding to apply.
expectations: Does not produce a Role or RoleBinding manifest

States that on an operator-managed instance the destination-namespace Role and RoleBinding are created by the operator from the argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by label or a completed NamespaceManagement handshake, and that a hand-written binding will not be adopted
Routes to skills/gitops/argo-operator for the diagnosis
Also checks the AppProject layer, noting that Kubernetes RBAC and AppProject restrictions are independent and both can reject a sync

evals.name: Manual-sync Application is not a fault
evals.prompt: Automated check: Application legacy-erp in namespace apps has been OutOfSync for 6 days. Diagnose it.
expectations: Checks spec.syncPolicy.automated before diagnosing anything
States that an Application with no automated policy is manual-sync and that sitting OutOfSync is its normal resting state, not a fault
Does not recommend enabling auto-sync, noting it is a policy decision that is often deliberate for production
Reports that no action is required rather than manufacturing a remediation

evals.name: Does not conflate diff state with operation state
evals.prompt: Application reporting is Synced but status.operationState.phase says Failed. Which one is right? Is my app broken?
expectations: Explains that the two fields describe different things: sync status is the result of the most recent comparison, and operationState.phase is the outcome of the last sync operation
States that both readings can be correct simultaneously, because a comparison after a failed sync can legitimately find no difference
Reads the syncResult per-resource messages to establish what actually failed rather than treating the pair as contradictory
Notes that the Application's health status is a separate question from either field

evals.name: PruneSkipped is not a failure
evals.prompt: After a sync, Application infra shows one resource with status PruneSkipped and the Application is still OutOfSync. The sync reported Succeeded. Is the sync broken, and should I turn on prune?
expectations: States that PruneSkipped is not a failure: the resource exists live, is no longer in git, and Argo CD was told not to delete it
Names the three reasons — automated.prune false by default, a Prune=false sync-option annotation, or an IgnoreExtraneous compare-option annotation — and checks which applies
States that enabling prune is destructive and affects every live resource in the Application no longer present in git, leaving the decision to a human
Does not recommend prune: true as a routine fix
